Bug_Title: DMI: Double.longBitsToDouble invoked on an int (DMI_LONG_BITS_TO_DOUBLE_INVOKED_ON_INT)
Bug_Details:
The Double.longBitsToDouble method is invoked, but a 32 bit int value is passed
    as an argument. This almost certainly is not intended and is unlikely
    to give the intended result.
Bug_Explanation: The Double.longBitsToDouble method is invoked, but a 32 bit int value is passed as an argument. This almost certainly is not intended and is unlikely to give the intended result.
Trigger_Explanation: The Double.longBitsToDouble method is invoked with an int argument. This will result in a Double.NaN value instead of the expected double. This is because the Double.longBitsToDouble method converts a long (64 bits) to a double, and an int (32 bits) is not large enough to represent the sign and exponent of a double. Hence, it results in Double.NaN.
